To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report the clinical, genetic and pathological findings in a new consanguineous INAD family from Senegal, and that we identified the first homozygous c.1483C>T mutation in PLA2G in an INAD family from West Africa.
we identified a homozygous missense mutation in PLA2G in a family from Senegal with infantile neuro-axonal dystrophy and that this mutation has not been described before in this disorder.
a new homozyggote mutation of the PLA2G6 (c.1482C>T) gene was detected in a Senegalese family affected by infantile neuroaxional dystrophy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical, histopathological, and genetic characterization of a new PLA2G mutation in a family from Senegal with INAD, a severe progressive neurodegenerative disease.
the genetic and clinical characterization of a consanguineous INAD family with a novel PLA2G6 variant.
the genetic basis of PLAN and its clinical implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLAN syndrome is a clinical spectrum of phenotypes with variable age at onset.
the clinical spectrum of PLA2G-associated NBIA is wider than previously thought.
PLAN syndrome is a heterogeneous disorder with variable age of onset and clinical features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutation c.1483C > T in the PLA2G6-gene is associated with the INAD-phenotype.
this study contributes to the understanding of the genotype-phenotypes correlations of PLA2G mutations.
this new PLA2G mutation (c.1485C>T) in a consanguineous family of Senegal with INAD, is the first to be described and the second to be reported in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of INAD should be considered in children with progressive motor impairment and neurodegeneration, even if they are not from consanguineous families.
the clinical diagnosis of INAD should be considered in patients with a history of developmental delay, spasticity and dystonia.
the clinical diagnosis of INAD should prompt genetic testing for PLA2G6 mutations.
